subject: Preflight: private Kubernetes footprint, eviction QoS, and encrypted blockstore requirements
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@novaclinic.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference
Date: 2026-05-30T09:12:00Z
Subject: Private deployment preflight — sizing + encryption + eviction questions

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We have two tracks to close before the signoff call next week: (1) exact cluster footprint (CPU/GPU mix, node counts per AZ), (2) storage encryption and snapshot/retention policy, and (3) expected pod eviction behavior under disk pressure.

We ran a quick spike and expect sustained 1k concurrent API sessions (short text prompts) and periodic batch embedding jobs that will spike CPU for an hour twice per day. We do not plan to run heavy training; inference-only. Our environment is locked down — HSM-backed KMS is a requirement and any customer-facing logs must be zero-retention by default.

Could you confirm a recommended baseline node pool mix (m-type / ssd vs nvme), preferred storage class settings for encrypted blockstore, and a proposal for kubelet eviction thresholds and eviction grace behavior we can test? Also please attach any preflight checklist you want us to complete (hardware imaging, network egress rules, MTU, BGP peering notes).

We attached our short preflight questions (novaclinic-preflight-questions.pdf).

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Patel
Director, Cloud Operations
NovaClinic

From: irene.choi@redwood.inference
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference, Sara Patel <sara@novaclinic.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.inference
Date: 2026-05-30T13:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment preflight — sizing + encryption + eviction questions

Sara / Rishi — long but actionable reply below. I focused on concrete primitives you can validate in a lab environment. I attached a draft runbook (redwood-private-deploy-runbook-draft.odt) and a small checklist spreadsheet.

1) Baseline node pools (in order of preference):
   - control-plane (3 nodes, t3.large equivalent, non-GPU, dedicated, small ephemeral NVMe for kubelet & logs)
   - inference-cpu (3–6 nodes, 16–32 vCPU, 128–256GB RAM, local NVMe recommended for model cache; use filesystem overlay to avoid double-write to blockstore)
   - inference-gpu (optional 1–2 nodes for low-latency priority traffic, e.g., A100/80GB or equivalent; schedule only critical routes)
   - batch-workers (2–4 nodes, cost-optimized (dense CPU), attach larger blockstore for ephemeral job outputs)

   Notes: start with 3 inference-cpu nodes and autoscale based on CPU/utilization windows. If embedding batches produce long tails, scale batch-workers independent of inference pool.

2) Storage classes & encryption:
   - Default: encrypted blockstore (CSI provisioner) with customer KMS (HSM-backed). Require envelope encryption: data keys stored locally, wrapped by KMS.
   - Primary PV class: fast-ssd-encrypted (thin-provisioned), ReclaimPolicy: Retain, fsType ext4 or xfs (xfs preferred for heavy IO).
   - Cache PVs: local-nvme (hostPath/LocalPV via CSI) for KV/prefix cache; ensure node affinity so pods land where cache exists. Local PVs should carry node-specific labels and not be replicated.
   - Snapshots: use CSI snapshotter; retention policy in checklist: daily snapshots with 7-day rolling retention by default, longer retention via archival to encrypted object store if required.

3) Kubelet eviction & QoS policy (recommended baseline):
   - Eviction thresholds (start conservative): 
       * evictionHard: memory.available<150Mi,nodefs.available<10%,nodefs.inodesFree<5%,imagefs.available<15%
       * evictionSoft: memory.available<300Mi,nodefs.available<20% with evictionSoftGracePeriod: "1m" for nodefs and 5m for memory
   - Disk pressure handling: prefer to evict best-effort pods first (QoS: BestEffort) and scale down batch-workers. For model cache eviction, implement controlled LRU at the application layer before relying on kubelet evictions.
   - PodPriority/Preemption: Define 'system-critical' and 'inference-critical' priority classes. Batch jobs run under lower priority to ensure tail latency for inference routes.

4) Acceptance tests (what we can provide):
   - Simulate node disk pressure: using fio + filling imagefs to replicate nodefs.available thresholds and observe pods evicted in expected order.
   - KMS/HSM integration test: wrap/unwrap cycle, key rotation test, and automatic unseal on restart.
   - Cold cache recovery: measure 95th percentile latency when cache is cold vs warmed.

5) Network & egress:
   - MTU: prefer 9000 on private interconnects; verify path MTU for customers with intermediate routers; Calico BGP peering recommended for islanded clusters.
   - Egress policy: restrict to required SaaS endpoints; implement NAT gateway with logging. Keep application logs out of egress path by default (zero-retention flagging).

6) Small operational checklist items (from the runbook):
   - Confirm KMS HSM model and credentials flow; share test key for validation.
   - Provide a small set (5–10) of canonical prompts we will use for quality/regression checks during rollout.
   - Confirm maintenance window for snapshot tests (we will exercise snapshot/restore during low-traffic window).

Attachments: redwood-private-deploy-runbook-draft.odt, deployment-checklist-v1.xlsx

If these defaults look OK to you, we will prepare a short acceptance test harness and a step-by-step lab guide for your ops team. Happy to refine thresholds after we see real IO characteristics.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Lead, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-private-deploy-runbook-draft.odt (application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.text)]

From: Sara Patel <sara@novaclinic.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.inference, rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference
Cc: ops@novaclinic.com
Date: 2026-05-31T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment preflight — sizing + encryption + eviction questions

Thanks, Irene — that level of detail is perfect. A couple clarifying points before we lock anything down: 

- HSM requirement: we run AWS CloudHSM in our VPC; any reference architecture needs to support a CloudHSM cluster and rotation workflow. Are your KMS integrations compatible with CloudHSM (we will provide access details)?
- Snapshots: we will accept 7-day rolling retention for fast recovery, but long-term archival must go to our encrypted S3 bucket under our account. Can the snapshot lifecycle be hooked to that policy?
- Eviction softGracePeriod: would you be comfortable increasing memory soft grace to 10m for our environment? We have occasional 8–10m spikebacks during chart imports.

If those are all achievable, please send the acceptance test plan and we can schedule the preflight lab for Wednesday morning.

Sara

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference
To: Sara Patel <sara@novaclinic.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.inference, marissa.cole@redwood.inference, neha.kapoor@redwood.inference
Date: 2026-05-31T10:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment preflight — sizing + encryption + eviction questions

Sara — great, thanks for the quick clarifications. Short answers: yes to CloudHSM (we support CloudHSM-backed KMS via envelope key wrapping), yes to exporting snapshots to your encrypted S3 (we'll add lifecycle hooks in the CSI controller), and we can set memory evictionSoftGracePeriod to 10m for the acceptance lab.

Action items and owners:
 - Irene: finalize acceptance test plan (KMS wrap/unwrap, disk-pressure evictions, snapshot->S3 restore). Deliver by 2026-06-01 EOD.
 - Marissa: send final runbook with imaging checklist and MTU/BGP guidance. Add a short section for network ACLs required from customer side. Deliver by 2026-06-01 EOD.
 - Neha: prepare the capacity estimate template (node counts, cost estimates across dedicated vs burst). Deliver by 2026-06-01 noon.
 - Sara / NovaClinic: provide CloudHSM test credentials and a lead contact for S3 lifecycle permissions.

I'll schedule the preflight lab for Wednesday 2026-06-02 09:00 PT and share a dial-in. Forward-looking note: we'll use the lab results to tune eviction thresholds and local NVMe sizing before finalizing the Dedicated capacity contract.

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
